# Plan: Sample

Feature: sample
Goal: Documentation fixture.
Max parallel: 2

| ID | Task | Depends on | Layer | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T01 | [Base](tasks/T01-base.md) | — | 1 | done |
| T02 | [Write result](tasks/T02-result.md) | T01 | 2 | pending |
| T03 | [Verify result](tasks/T03-verify.md) | T01, T02 | 3 | pending |

## Extension decisions

Extend the existing plan: copy the seed from project-root base.txt into result.txt,
preserving its bytes (currently `seed` followed by a newline). Only result.txt is
an implementation write target. Final verification is read-only. No unresolved
decisions. [Research and approach](research.md).

## Execution

No active writers. T01 accepted by fixture author; base.txt contains the required seed.

Planning extension: T02 and T03 added as pending legacy tasks. T01 and its evidence
remain unchanged. Layers: T01 → T02 → T03. No implementation dispatched.

north/plans/sample/research.md.text:
---
type: Research
title: Sample seed-copy extension
description: Local evidence and selected approach for extending the legacy sample plan.
sources:
  - id: base
    resource: ../../../base.txt
  - id: prior-task
    resource: tasks/T01-base.md
---
# Approach

Plan: [Sample](index.md).

Question: How should T02 produce the requested seed result while preserving T01?
The input is exactly `seed` plus a newline.[^base] T01 records acceptance of that
input and no active writer.[^prior-task]

Select a direct byte-preserving copy from base.txt to result.txt. Hardcoding the
seed is unnecessary and would not derive the output from the requested source.
No library, external research, or experiment is needed for this bounded file copy.
T02 depends on T01; read-only T03 verifies the combined result after T02 acceptance.
There are no unresolved approach decisions. This is planning evidence, not proof
that result.txt has been created or checked. No relevant saved memories or local
preference skills were present in the inspected fixture.

[^base]: Project-root base.txt inspected during planning.
[^prior-task]: Existing legacy T01 metadata and acceptance evidence, preserved in place.

north/plans/sample/tasks/T01-base.md.text:
---
id: T01
status: done
depends_on: []
agent: north-worker
write_scope: [base.txt]
custom_evidence: retain-original
---
# Base

Plan: [Sample](../index.md)
Outcome: Seed is available in base.txt.
Acceptance: base.txt contains seed.
Execution: Supplied and accepted in fixture setup. No active writer.

north/plans/sample/tasks/T02-result.md.text:
---
id: T02
status: pending
depends_on: [T01]
agent: north-worker
write_scope: [result.txt]
---
# Write result

Plan: [Sample](../index.md)
Prerequisites: [T01](T01-base.md).
Outcome: Project-root result.txt contains the seed read from base.txt, with bytes preserved.
Acceptance: From the project root, `cmp base.txt result.txt` succeeds; base.txt remains unchanged and contains `seed` followed by a newline. Only result.txt is changed by this task.
Execution: Not dispatched. No changed files or validation results yet. No known blockers beyond T01 acceptance.

north/plans/sample/tasks/T03-verify.md.text:
---
id: T03
status: pending
depends_on: [T01, T02]
agent: north-verifier
write_scope: []
---
# Verify result

Plan: [Sample](../index.md)
Prerequisites: [T01](T01-base.md), [T02](T02-result.md).
Outcome: Read-only final verification of the accepted seed and result.
Acceptance: Review T01/T02 acceptance evidence and read base.txt and result.txt; confirm both contain exactly `seed` followed by a newline. Confirm `cmp base.txt result.txt` succeeds and base.txt retains its original SHA-256 `4a6689419b00b11700c9b6246bcfa8936c8f5e1e824db3a7e57030e2d1c1a684`. Report findings without writing files; primary records any execution evidence.
Execution: Not dispatched. No verification performed. Waiting for T02 acceptance.

assets/skills/north-plan/SKILL.md.text:
---
name: north-plan
description: Turn a feature request into a linked Markdown dependency plan using requirements clarification, saved memory, and exploration. Use for /north-plan or creating and revising a North implementation plan.
---

# North plan

Plan the user's requested outcome without implementing the feature.

Load `north-sources` for the artifact root and read its
[OKF profile](../north-sources/references/okf-format.md) and
[plan contract](../north-sources/references/plan-format.md). Load `invoke-memory`
for relevant prior implementation knowledge, then `clarify-requirements` for
the agreed behavior, acceptance examples, and consequential unanswered questions.
Use existing project instructions and OpenSpec requirements as context.

Load `north-explore` to compare implementation approaches. Use its recommendation,
constraints, and evidence gaps to shape the work. Record unresolved decisions
against the tasks they block; this phase can save a partial plan without
inventing the user's answer.

## Build the feature plan

Choose a short lowercase hyphenated feature slug. Reuse the same feature's
existing plan; use a distinct slug when a name belongs to unrelated work.
For a new feature, create the navigation-only `index.md`, detailed `plan.md`,
research record, and task files defined by the plan contract. Use `type: North Plan`
and `type: North Task` with `north_schema: north-plan-v1` on plan/tasks, and
`type: Research` on research. The overview owns the task table; the index lists
the overview, research, and actual tasks (or their directory listing).
Link existing requirements and research rather than copying them.

For existing plans, select the actual authority using the contract, including
legacy detailed indexes and single-file plans. Revisions do not implicitly
convert them. Preserve unknown metadata, provenance, history, and incoming links;
explicit conversion follows the contract. Apply the profile's reserved-name,
evidence, and meaningful-update rules without inventing verification.

Split work at real dependency boundaries. Give each task a concrete outcome,
allowed write scope, and observable acceptance checks. Include dependencies
caused by reads of unfinished contracts, generated outputs, or shared resources.
Keep task-local tests with their implementation when practical; do not add tasks
just to create parallel activity. Include a final integration verification task
depending on every implementation branch.

Validate the graph and compute its layers using the contract. In a new-schema
plan, added tasks start with `task_status: pending`, or `task_status: blocked`
with the consequential decision or missing evidence. When extending a legacy
plan, added tasks retain that plan's legacy execution format (`status` in legacy
directory task files, or the existing single-file table); do not introduce a
new-schema task into its legacy authority. This explicit compatibility exception
does not convert the plan or certify it as OKF. In new-schema records, OKF
`status` is lifecycle, not task progress.
A delegated `north-planner` returns proposed contents for the primary to save.
Record any project-required synchronization with external task artifacts.

## Handoff

Summarize the planned outcome, chosen approach, layers, and blocked decisions.
Link the authoritative overview (new `plan.md`, legacy index or single file),
optionally its navigation index, and suggest `/north-execute <feature>` after those decisions
are resolved. For read-only planning, return proposed contents and paths and
state that saving the plan is still needed before execution.

assets/skills/north-sources/references/p.text:
# North plan contract

Use the artifact root resolved by `north-sources` and the
[OKF v0.2 profile](okf-format.md). New feature plans use:

```text
north/plans/account-settings/
  index.md
  plan.md
  research.md
  tasks/
    T01-contract.md
    T02-endpoint.md
    T03-form.md
    T04-integration.md
```

The primary agent is the only editor of the shared plan. Each task file's
frontmatter is authoritative for task metadata and status; its body holds
acceptance and execution evidence. `plan.md` owns the overview and synchronized
task table; `index.md` is only navigation (see the profile's listing example).
Reconcile a stale table against task files and actual execution before dispatch.
These Markdown conventions guide an agent; there is no automatic scheduler.

## Plan example (`plan.md`)

```markdown
---
type: North Plan
north_schema: north-plan-v1
title: Account settings
description: Plan for viewing and updating a display name.
---
# Plan: Account settings

Feature: account-settings
Goal: Users can view and update their display name.
Context: Link relevant requirements, code, and applicable saved memory here.
Acceptance: A valid name persists; invalid input shows an error without changing it.
Non-goals: Account deletion and email changes.
Max parallel: 2
Research: [Findings and decisions](research.md)

## Tasks

| ID | Task | Depends on | Layer | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T01 | [Define contract](tasks/T01-contract.md) | — | 1 | pending |
| T02 | [Implement endpoint](tasks/T02-endpoint.md) | T01 | 2 | pending |
| T03 | [Implement form](tasks/T03-form.md) | T01 | 2 | pending |
| T04 | [Verify integration](tasks/T04-integration.md) | T02, T03 | 3 | pending |

## Decisions and open questions

Record settled requirements, assumptions, and unresolved decisions with affected IDs.

## Execution and handoff

Record the project root, resolved North path, source branch and starting commit
when applicable, existing local changes, active layer, session/worktree references,
and integration results. Keep revisions, retry reasons, and unfinished IDs here.
Link saved implementation memory after /north-save.
```

## Task example

Use one file per task. `depends_on` holds IDs, not titles or unchecked prose.
`write_scope` uses project-relative paths; an empty list means read-only.

```markdown
---
type: North Task
north_schema: north-plan-v1
id: T02
task_status: pending
depends_on: [T01]
agent: north-worker
write_scope: [src/server/settings/, tests/server/settings/]
---

# T02: Implement settings endpoint

Plan: [Account settings](../plan.md)
Prerequisites: [T01: Contract](T01-contract.md)
Research: [Findings](../research.md)

## Outcome

Persist the authenticated user's display name using the agreed contract.

## Acceptance

- A valid update is returned by a subsequent read.
- An invalid name returns the agreed validation error and leaves stored data unchanged.
- Run the project's focused endpoint checks; record exact commands and outcomes.

## Execution

Dispatch/session: Not dispatched.
Checkout/branch/base commit: Not assigned; record if using worktrees.
Changed files: None yet.
Validation: None yet.
Review/integration: Not reviewed or integrated.
Blockers: None known.

## History

Record dispatch, outcomes, repairs, and evidence invalidated by later changes.
```

Replace example paths with actual project paths. Root tasks use `depends_on: []`
and `Prerequisites: None`. A final review task can use `north-verifier` and
`write_scope: []`; the primary runs checks the read-only verifier cannot run.
Do not mark a task complete based only on its worker's report.

`research.md` uses `type: Research`, links back to `plan.md`, and records the question, repository and
external evidence, alternatives considered, selected approach, applicability,
and unresolved gaps. It is context, not an executable task. Link to relevant
research already stored elsewhere instead of duplicating it.

## Graph validation

Task IDs are stable and unique. Every dependency names an existing task, required
execution references and local evidence claimed as existing resolve, and the graph
has no cycles or self-dependencies. Dangling optional knowledge links are tolerated
by OKF; they do not waive missing North execution prerequisites.
Write scopes and acceptance checks must describe real project paths and
observable outcomes. Include semantic dependencies such as reads of unfinished
contracts, generated outputs, lockfiles, and shared test resources.

Use a positive `Max parallel` value, defaulting to 2. Compute the plan table's layers
from dependencies: roots are layer 1; each other task is one layer after its
latest prerequisite. Recompute after graph revisions. The execution workflow
decides when a layer may start; `north-execute` owns pipeline layer barriers.

## Status and evidence

New-format plan/task records require `north_schema: north-plan-v1`. This discriminator
selects the North execution contract independently of OKF version and `type`.
Tasks require a non-empty `id`, `task_status` from the table below, `depends_on`
as an ID list, a named `agent`, and `write_scope` as a project-relative path list
(empty means read-only), plus actionable outcome, acceptance, and evidence sections.
`type: North Task` alone is not permission to execute an incomplete record.
Unknown schemas remain readable but require clarification before dispatch.

For this schema, `status` is optional OKF lifecycle (`draft`, `stable`,
`deprecated`), never execution progress. Omit it unless useful; its default
`stable` implies no execution completion or verification. Preserve lifecycle,
provenance, and unknown extension fields while updating `task_status`.

| Task status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| pending | Not dispatched, possibly waiting for prerequisites. |
| running | Dispatch recorded; execution is being launched or is active. |
| needs-review | Work returned; acceptance and integration still need review. |
| done | Primary reviewed the result and acceptance evidence; accepted changes are available to dependents. |
| blocked | Failure, unresolved decision, or uncertain execution requires resolution. |

Record dispatch before launch, adding the native session reference when available.
Keep changed files, exact checks and results, missing evidence, review findings,
and integration state in the task's execution section. A worker report or status
label alone is not completion evidence. Synchronize plan table entries from task files;
preserve previous outcomes and reasons for repairs in the history.

If project instructions also require an external progress artifact such as
OpenSpec tasks, record its location and synchronize it from verified outcomes.

## Select and resume a plan

An explicit selector may be a feature name, plan directory, index or plan path, or legacy
single-file plan. Otherwise use an unambiguous plan from the conversation, or a
sole plan matching the requested phase. Ask when several match; do not choose
by modification time. If none exists, identify the missing plan.

Select authority by layout and metadata, not by filename alone:

| Evidence | Authority and progress field |
| --- | --- |
| New directory: `plan.md` declares `north-plan-v1`; task records declare it too | `plan.md` overview; tasks own `task_status`; `index.md` only lists files. |
| Legacy directory: `index.md` is the existing detailed plan with task table and links to legacy task records | That index remains overview; positively identified legacy tasks own execution `status`. |
| Legacy single-file plan | Its task table owns metadata/execution status; detail sections own evidence. |
| Navigation index only | Follow its plan link; missing overview/tasks block execution, not reading. |
| Competing single-file/directory or two detailed overviews | Ask for authoritative selection unless an explicit selector or recorded conversion resolves it. Do not merge or choose newest. |

When extending a selected legacy plan without explicit conversion, create added
tasks in that same legacy format: directory tasks keep execution `status` and
the existing metadata/body structure, without adding `north_schema` or OKF
lifecycle fields; single-file plans gain rows and detail sections in place.
Keep their detailed index or single file authoritative, and preserve existing
IDs, extensions, evidence, and history. This compatibility exception to new
artifact formatting keeps ordinary revisions resumable; it does not make the
legacy plan OKF-conformant. Do not mix new-schema tasks into a legacy authority.

Do not infer legacy task state from an arbitrary concept's `status`. Identify a
legacy task by its membership in a legacy plan and its existing ID, dependency,
agent, scope, acceptance, and execution structure. Missing required fields block
dispatch until resolved, not a reset to pending. `task_status` without the schema,
a new-schema record with `status: pending`/`running`/etc., conflicting duplicated
state, or a schema/layout mismatch is ambiguous: report and clarify before writes
or dispatch. A new-schema `task_status: pending` plus `status: draft` is valid.

Before continuing, compare task records and the authoritative overview with the checkout,
validation evidence, and available native sessions, worktrees, and commits.
Establish that a prior writer has stopped before retrying a `running` task.
Unknown execution state is a blocker, not permission to launch a second writer.
Review partial work, preserve user changes, and repair a stale task table in its
existing authority. Reading/resuming does not convert the format or create indexes.

Recheck completed results against the current implementation. If a prerequisite
changes, invalidate affected downstream completion evidence and record which
tasks need review or reexecution. Revalidate the graph after revisions. Keep
plan paths and unfinished IDs in handoffs.

## Explicit conversion only

An existing `north/plans/<feature>.md` remains authoritative when resuming.
Its task table owns metadata/status and its detail sections hold evidence.
Apply this contract without rewriting history or creating a competing plan.
The same preservation rule applies to legacy directory plans, including the
bootstrap plan for this format change. New features use the new directory layout;
convert existing plans only on an explicit format-update/migration request.

Before conversion, establish that active writers have stopped. Record the old
authority and inventory incoming links/anchors. Preserve IDs, dependencies,
scopes, acceptance, history, dispatch references, and evidence. Move the detailed
directory overview from `index.md` to `plan.md`, replace the index with navigation,
and update known overview links (task-file links can remain stable). For a
single-file conversion, preserve a typed compatibility record at the old path
with useful historical anchors and a link to the new authority; do not leave two
active task tables. If incoming anchors cannot be preserved safely, report the
limit and agree a link repair before conversion.

Add `type` and `north_schema` to converted plan/tasks; move each unambiguous legacy
execution `status` to `task_status`, not to lifecycle. Do not invent lifecycle or
verification. Resolve ambiguous values before conversion. Preserve research and
other records unless explicitly included; identify any remaining legacy files
as a mixed bundle. Recheck graph, paths, selectors, and progress equivalence after
conversion; a reserved-name collision is not permission to overwrite content.

assets/skills/north-sources/references/o.text:
# North OKF v0.2 profile

Format authority: [OKF v0.2 specification](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/open-knowledge-format/blob/ad30107c31c06aec8a7d5636e0d1058118604e6f/SPEC.md)
(pinned commit `ad30107c31c06aec8a7d5636e0d1058118604e6f`). This is a file
convention, not a new skill, validator, or runtime dependency.

## Boundary and concepts

The resolved North output directory is one bundle, including generated local
`skills/*/SKILL.md`. Apply this profile to newly saved project artifacts, not
bundled kit skills/commands, repository documentation, code, or authoritative
requirements such as OpenSpec. Link those sources where they already live.
Any non-reserved `.md` file inside the bundle counts when assessing conformance;
legacy or foreign files are not silently exempted by their origin.

A concept is UTF-8 Markdown starting with `---`-delimited, parseable YAML mapping
frontmatter and a Markdown body. Its only always-required field is a non-empty
string `type`. Its identity is its bundle path without `.md`; a task's `id` is
a separate North identifier. Use meaningful `title` and one-sentence `description`
when known; `resource` (canonical asset URI) and `tags` are optional. Unknown
types and extension keys are valid; preserve them during updates.

North's descriptive types (not an OKF registry):

| Artifact | `type` |
| --- | --- |
| Plan overview / task | `North Plan` / `North Task` |
| Research / implementation memory | `Research` / `Implementation Memory` |
| Preference record / generated skill | `Preference Observation` / `Agent Skill` |
| Continuation / experiment | `Handoff` / `Prototype` |
| Evaluation / retrospective | `Skill Evaluation` / `Retrospective` |
| Supporting requirements / domain / architecture notes | `Requirements` / `Domain Model` / `Architecture Review` |

Other saved records may choose another descriptive type. North-specific keys,
including `north_schema`, `id`, `depends_on`, `agent`, `write_scope`,
`task_status`, and `preference_status`, are extensions. Do not overload OKF fields
with workflow state. See [the plan contract](plan-format.md) for executable plans.

## Reserved files and lazy navigation

`index.md` and `log.md` are reserved at **every** directory level, never concept
slugs. Choose a different descriptive slug for a concept named index or log;
report an existing collision instead of overwriting or silently renaming it.

Indexes are optional heading-grouped Markdown link listings with descriptions,
not detailed plan overviews or task/memory tables. They have no frontmatter,
except the bundle-root `index.md` may contain only `okf_version: "0.2"`.
For example, at the bundle root:

```markdown
---
okf_version: "0.2"
---
# Plans

- [Account settings](plans/account-settings/) - Plan, research, and tasks.

# Memories

- [Implementation memories](memories/) - Saved coverage and evidence.
```

At `plans/account-settings/index.md` (no frontmatter):

```markdown
# Account settings

- [Plan](plan.md) - Goal, decisions, task graph, and execution handoff.
- [Research](research.md) - Evidence and selected approach.
- [Contract task](tasks/T01-contract.md) - Define the settings contract.
- [Endpoint task](tasks/T02-endpoint.md) - Implement the settings endpoint.
```

List every actual task or link to a task-directory listing. Memory indexes
similarly list memory concepts; coverage belongs in those concepts, optionally
summarized in descriptions. Do not create links to nonexistent artifacts as
though they already exist. Examples here describe hypothetical saved files.

Optional `log.md` uses a flat list of prose entries grouped under ISO date
headings (`## 2026-11-05`), newest first, with links to changes; no concept
frontmatter. These date headings are dates, not timestamp-valued metadata.

Lookup/resume creates no navigation. `/north` creates only the output directory.
When saving, create/update relevant listings lazily, preserve unrelated entries,
and serialize shared navigation through the primary agent. A missing index is
never a reason to reject a bundle or block a known plan path.

## Links and evidence

Author file-relative Markdown links by default. Consumers also support `/`-prefixed
bundle-root links: from `memories/account-settings.md`, both
`../plans/account-settings/plan.md` and `/plans/account-settings/plan.md` identify
the same concept. Do not interpret the latter as a filesystem or repository path.
Resolve relative path-valued fields from the containing document as well;
`resource` and `sources[].resource` accept URLs, bundle-root paths, or relative
paths. Source scope descriptors are not paths and need not resolve.

Relative references that leave the bundle, such as `../../src/settings.ts` from
that memory, are project evidence, not portable bundle concept edges. Check
local evidence claimed to exist against the checkout; report missing evidence.
Exporting North alone does not include external code, OpenSpec, or remote sources.
Do not copy authority merely to make an export self-contained. An optional
`references/` directory may hold deliberately saved material; its Markdown
concepts follow the same rules. Links express relationships through their prose.

## Provenance, trust, freshness, lifecycle

All these families are optional. Omit unknown facts rather than fill templates
with invented actors, timestamps, verification, counts, or source dates.

- `sources` is a list; each entry requires `resource`. Add a stable `id` when
  citing it. A claim's footnote label joins to that exact `sources[].id`, not
  its list position or the footnote prose. Preserve IDs when reordering sources.
- `generated` records authorship of current content, with required `by` and a
  known last meaningful change time in `at` when available. `verified` records
  actual confirmation against sources/resource: events with `by` and `at`.
  Accept either a list or one mapping (normalize the mapping as a one-item list).
- Actors use `<producer>/<version>` for agents/tools, `human:<id>` for people,
  or `process:<id>` for processes. Use actual identities only. Agent authorship,
  a passing code test, or `task_status: done` does not itself verify a document.
- No `verified` means unverified; non-human verifiers mean machine-confirmed;
  a `human:` verifier means human-reviewed. These are derived advisory signals,
  not stored credibility scores or access-control grants. Retain history but
  identify verification invalidated by content changes; do not imply reconfirmation.
- `status` is only `draft`, `stable`, or `deprecated`; absent means `stable`
  under OKF, not reviewed, verified, or implemented. `stale_after` is an optional
  absolute instant; stale means now is at or after it.
- Every timestamp-valued field uses ISO 8601 with explicit UTC offset, e.g.
  `2026-11-05T10:00:00Z` or `2026-11-05T12:00:00+02:00`, never a date alone or
  naive local time. Quote timestamps if needed to preserve their string form.
- Source `author`, `last_modified`, and `usage_count` are optional observed facts.
  Counts use a known `usage_window: {from, to}` alongside `sources` (or an
  entry-specific override), not fabricated popularity. No attestation runtime
  is introduced; preserve unfamiliar computation fields and consult pinned §10
  before authoring an `Attested Computation` (which also requires `runtime`).

## Concept examples

These are illustrative templates, not evidence of completed implementation.
Only include source links and coverage assertions supported by the actual save.
For `plans/account-settings/research.md`:

```markdown
---
type: Research
title: Account settings research
description: Contract options and remaining evidence gaps.
sources:
  - id: contract
    resource: tasks/T01-contract.md
---
# Findings

The contract task defines the acceptance questions.[^contract]
Plan: [Account settings](plan.md).

[^contract]: Contract task and its acceptance criteria.
```

For `memories/account-settings.md`, after reviewing only the contract:

```markdown
---
type: Implementation Memory
title: Account settings contract
description: Contract coverage only; endpoint implementation remains unverified.
sources:
  - id: contract
    resource: /plans/account-settings/tasks/T01-contract.md
---
# Coverage

This record covers the contract, not endpoint completion.[^contract]
See the [plan](../plans/account-settings/plan.md) for remaining tasks.

[^contract]: Contract task; check its acceptance evidence against current code.
```

For `skills/focused-checks/SKILL.md`, only after the preference owner's required
observations support promotion:

```markdown
---
type: Agent Skill
name: focused-checks
description: Use focused checks when validating a bounded change.
---
# Focused checks

Run checks scoped to the changed behavior before broader validation.
Evidence: [Preference observations](../../dry/focused-checks.md).
```

Keep native skill `name`/`description` and direct local consumption; this profile
does not claim compatibility with every third-party skill validator. Preference
observations use `type: Preference Observation` and their owner's
`preference_status` extension, not OKF `status` for promotion progress.

## Compatibility and truthful reporting

Read legacy records in place; preserve provenance, extensions, history, and
incoming references. An explicit format update may adapt the selected record;
ordinary reading or progress updates do not mandate conversion. Never bulk
migrate unrelated records or infer conversion from a version declaration.
Use the plan contract's selection/conversion rules for live plans. Its explicit
legacy-extension exception keeps added tasks in the selected legacy format until
conversion is requested; those records remain legacy, not OKF-certified output.

Claim full bundle conformance only after checking **every** non-reserved Markdown
file has parseable frontmatter with non-empty `type`, and all reserved files
follow their defined structure. A root version targets a spec, not certification.
Report legacy/new mixtures as mixed; distinguish checked files from unchecked
bundle contents and static checks from observed writer/consumer behavior.

Consumers tolerate missing optional fields, unknown types/extensions, missing
indexes, and dangling cross-links. Missing trust is not grounds for rejection.
This tolerance does not authorize North execution with missing task metadata,
unresolved required prerequisites, or uncertain writer state: block dispatch,
not general reading. Nor does it excuse claiming a broken evidence link was
validated. An unfamiliar declared OKF version calls for best-effort reading,
not silent rewriting or a claim of verified conformance.
